integrityVerdict.evidence: T1/T4/T11/T12: existing Party workspace, shared Button/Input/Dialog/AppSelect/payment editor and source handlers remain. The new tab hook and print rules are Party-local; unchanged validators and payload construction are visible in all five affected dialogs.

problems.evidence: T7/T9 and guide §§7/14/30. Payment submit at53–57 sets only a bottom error string; amount80, discount88, reason95 and split consumer97 have no error IDs, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, or failed-submit focus. Alert106 announces feedback but is not focusable or associated with the affected controls. Refund45–49/77/87/97 repeats the gap; Finance51–61/84/105 does so after existing validators; Opening50–55/77/90 and correction/reversal42–56/85/90/98/107 likewise have no association or recovery focus. Source checked directly at the stated revision; no browser or assistive-technology outcome is inferred.
problems.fix: Preserve all current validators, their order/messages, calculations, payloads, submit/catch behavior and draft values. Add Party-local presentation error state, stable translated field/error associations and focus to the first deterministically invalid control after local review/save failure; use a focusable existing error summary for a submission/domain error that cannot safely identify a field. Expose narrow opt-in split-field props only where needed, with shared Finance defaults unchanged. Cover payment amount/discount/reason/splits, refund, finance, opening, and correction/reversal recovery.

problems.evidence: T7/T12 and guide §§9/30. PartyPaymentDialog97, PartyCreditRefundDialog90, PartyFinanceDialog94–95 and PartyTransactionDialog94–95 consume FinancePaymentSplitEditor. Its Input at src/components/finance/FinancePaymentSplitEditor.tsx:87–93 has only value, decimal mode, class, change handler and numeric placeholder; the row59 is a div, with no connected label/id/aria-label/aria-labelledby. Input.tsx24–25 routes it to NumericInput; NumericInput.tsx48 forwards supplied props to the real input and only uses its inferred label on steppers59–61. Thus the actual split amount has no meaningful accessible name, including in source correction. No runtime accessible-tree assertion is claimed.
problems.fix: Add a narrowly optional presentation API to the shared split editor and opt in only from Party payment, refund, finance and correction consumers. Each amount must have a translated task/row-specific accessible name for one and multiple rows. Keep default markup/behavior for all other consumers, row values, method/account choices, normalization, parsers, validators and calculations unchanged. Coordinate error description/invalid state with the related validation finding.

summary: Official detector completed with zero findings. Source inspection confirms the round-two print, tab, Reset, Notes target and proportional-figure repairs, with no newly verified scoped regression; two stableP1 accessible-form issues remain. The coarse source-only14/20 score does not certify runtime accessibility, performance, themes, responsive behavior or print output.
openQuestions: After the narrow repair, exercise local failures and caught submission failures in payment/refund/finance/opening/correction/reversal; verify IDs, invalid state, correct focus target, preserved values, unchanged review/confirm semantics and translated output.
Inspect actual accessible names for single and multi-row split amounts in all four Party consumers, and prove that unrelated Finance/POS/Purchase consumers retain the default shared behavior.

Independent browser evidence must establish complete/multi-page PDFs, real tab keyboard selection/reveal, note target geometry, reset adjacency, computed proportional figures, both themes/languages, zoom and required responsive widths. This source audit neither reproduces nor replaces those results.
